fields.label: Intro sentence
paragraphs: A moulded rubber one-way flap that lets cabin air out and nothing back in. It relieves the pressure the HVAC blower builds, lets a slammed door close cleanly, and seals against water, dust, fumes and road noise the moment the pressure drops. Soft enough to lift at almost nothing — typically 40–50 Shore A.

Opening pressure and sealing at rest are the two halves of the specification, and they pull against each other: a flap free enough to vent easily is a flap that can be pushed open by wind or a pressure washer. Naming both, and asking for both, is what shows the supplier has built one before.

sections.title: Rubber compound options
sections.chip: Right default · but two options will perish
sections.live: LIVE → EPDM (SELECTED), NBR, Neoprene, SBR — correct default, and two compounds that crack on an exposed part

fields.label: The default is right; the menu is not
paragraphs: EPDM is pre-selected and it is the correct compound for an exposed ventilation flap — ozone, UV and water resistance, and it stays flexible at −40 °C, which is when a flap most needs to open. Do not let the developer change it.

🛑 The problem is the other three-quarters of the menu. NBR and SBR both have poor ozone and UV resistance, and this part spends its life behind a bumper or in a quarter panel. Offering them unranked invites a buyer to choose on price and get a flap that hardens and splits within a couple of seasons.
Margo produces every part in every compound it mixes (client-instructed 2026-09-02). Nothing is removed — all eight are ranked, and the two unsuitable ones are marked with the reason.

fields.label: Cards ×4
rows: The flap lifts on cabin pressure and drops the instant it falls. Get that balance wrong and you either trap air — heavy doors, weak vents — or let water and fumes back in. We tune it with thickness and hardness, not guesswork.
🛑 It has to work at −30 °C too
Rubber stiffens as it cools, and a flap that will not lift on a winter morning makes doors hard to close. EPDM is our default here because it stays soft cold — not just because it resists weather.
An extractor flap that flutters at speed is a warranty complaint, not a leak. Flap thickness, hardness and seat geometry decide it — tell us the airflow and we will tune the three together.
Exposed for the life of the vehicle

Behind a bumper the flap sees rain, road spray, sunlight and ozone. Nitrile and SBR crack in those conditions — we mix EPDM for this part, and we will say so even when a cheaper compound is asked for.
fields.note:
Four cards, four cards — no count change and no new element.
Card 03 is the one an OEM engineer will recognise. Flutter noise is the complaint that comes back from the field, it is not a sealing failure, and a supplier who raises it unprompted is a supplier who has been through the loop before.
Card 04 declines a sale in advance — it names the two compounds on Margo’s own live selector that should not be used here

sections.title: From compound to certification
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Certification · six steps · “compression moulding” is right on this page

fields.label: Steps
rows: Material compounding — polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. Hardness is set here, and on a flap it is the specification.
Mould design and CNC tool manufacture, in-house, held as a controlled record. The flap and its seat are cut together — the seat geometry is half of the sealing performance.
Compression moulding — [no change; correct on this part]
Post-cure and deflashing — flash removed from the flap edge and the seat. Flash on a sealing edge holds the valve open.
Quality inspection — hardness, flap thickness and opening pressure checked on batch samples, plus dimensional check.
Export packaging — industrial packing with documentation. Flaps packed flat and uncompressed — a flap stored folded takes a set and will not seal. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber is used.
fields.note:
Six steps, six kept — the process is right and four steps gain the detail that makes it specific.
Step 04 is the one worth the clause. On most mouldings flash is cosmetic; on a valve seat it holds the flap off its seat and the part leaks from new — and it is invisible unless someone is looking for it.
Step 05 turns opening pressure from a claim into an inspection, which is what makes the rest of the sheet credible

notes: The process block must render from the part record — right here by luck, not by data.
